executive_assessment.text: Kalinago livelihood dependence and named April 2026 impact sites deepen local vulnerabilities; the 2017 shelter snapshot remains historical.
Post-Maria unrest is a bounded historical disaster-security mechanism. Water/monitoring outputs and Kalinago inputs add capacity without proving durable protection or cohesion.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2017-11-15 reports: The PDNA reports about 500 artisans in the Kalinago Territory; around 98% had workspaces damaged or destroyed, and some also lost craft stock. Craft sales were a major Indigenous-community income source.

Source dated 2023-09-26 reports: DVRP’s 31-km East Coast Road works include slope/landslide stabilization, flood mitigation and bridge/culvert works; the route carries farm produce and connects the Kalinago community to services and tourist sites.

Source dated 2025-07-31 reports: The project document describes eight Kalinago hamlets under communal land governance; it cites a 2015 poverty assessment finding 50% of residents poor and notes reliance on agriculture and forest products vulnerable to ecosystem degradation and climate hazards.

Source dated 2025-07-31 reports: The project identifies communal-land compensation contention and political instability as risks; it plans a Council-controlled greenhouse site and community-led activities, with stronger Kalinago social cohesion an intended long-term outcome.

Source dated 2026-08-15 reports: UNDP reports 36 Kalinago Territory households received seedlings, fruit trees, tools, tarpaulins, water-storage equipment and climate-smart agriculture training through SCR-K; delivery was coordinated with the Kalinago Council and IsraAID Dominica.

Source dated 2026-05-01 reports: After a trough caused flooding and landslides, the government reported impacts in Antrizzle, Atkinson, the Kalinago Territory and Castle Bruce, including low-pressure water service, blocked farm access and crop/livestock losses; water and road restoration and farm inputs were under way.

Source dated 2026-05-01 reports: Rapid assessments identified 22 affected households comprising 64 people in Atkinson and Antrizzle; food packages were distributed with DEXIA and the Red Cross, and psychosocial support was provided.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification. Routine/default app-use approval does not certify claims or sources. 18 of 18 evidence records and 1 of 1 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.
No countrywide causal estimate of climate impacts on conflict or violence is established by these sources.

No inspected source attributes armed conflict or sustained political violence in Dominica to climate hazards. The government strategy does report limited post-Maria looting and social unrest, without characterizing it as armed conflict.

The first Biennial Transparency Report PDF was returned as a timeout and the Green Climate Fund adaptation-planning page as access denied; neither was used for claims. The UN human-security country assessment PDF was also inaccessible and not used.
The UNDP project document cites older poverty context and presents social cohesion and resilience gains as prospective; these are not evaluated outcomes.

No source inspected documents actual conflict or insecurity blocking climate-adaptation delivery; political instability appears only as a prospective project risk, while immediate recovery constraints are documented separately.
